turns.prompt_text: I own a Mac Mini, and a Macbook air, I would like to operate one along with the other via the same set of mouse & keyboard, I own a logitech Wave MK670 Combo with the mouse
turns.response_html:
Since you are using two Apple computers (a Mac Mini and a MacBook Air), you have a distinct advantage. You do not need to buy new hardware or worry about the specific limitations of your Logitech mouse.

The best solution is a built-in Apple feature called Universal Control.

The Problem with the Hardware Method

While your Logitech Wave Keys keyboard has "Easy-Switch" buttons (the F1, F2, F3 keys) to toggle between devices, the Signature M550 L mouse included in the MK670 combo is typically a single-device mouse. It does not have a toggle button to switch between computers.

If you relied on hardware switching, you would be able to switch your keyboard instantly, but your mouse would be "stuck" on one computer unless you physically moved the USB dongle or constantly re-paired it via Bluetooth.

The Solution: Apple Universal Control

Universal Control allows you to use your single keyboard and mouse to control both Macs seamlessly. You don't need to press any buttons to switch; you simply push your cursor to the edge of one screen, and it "hops" over to the other Mac.

Prerequisites:

  • Both Macs must be on macOS Monterey 12.4 or later.
  • Both Macs must be signed into the same iCloud account with Two-Factor Authentication enabled.
  • Both Macs must have Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, and Handoff turned on.
  • The devices must be near each other (within 30 feet).

How to Set It Up:

  1. Connect your Logitech Dongle: Plug the Logi Bolt receiver into the Mac Mini (or pair both the keyboard and mouse to the Mac Mini via Bluetooth). Ensure both function correctly on that one computer.
  2. Enable on Mac Mini:
    • Go to System Settings (or System Preferences) > Displays.
    • Click the Advanced button (or "Universal Control..." on older macOS versions).
    • Turn on: "Allow your pointer and keyboard to move between any nearby Mac or iPad."
  3. Enable on MacBook Air: Repeat the exact same step on your MacBook Air.
  4. Connect: Once enabled on both, push your mouse cursor against the edge of your screen (usually the side where your other Mac is physically located). You should see a small animation on the edge of the other screen "catching" the cursor. Push through, and you are now controlling the second Mac.

Alternative: Software KVMs

If Universal Control is not working for you (e.g., you are on a restricted work VPN that blocks iCloud features), you can use third-party software that mimics this behavior over your local network:

  • ShareMouse: Easy to set up, drag-and-drop file sharing.
  • Synergy: A classic paid option, very robust for software engineers.
  • Barrier: An open-source, free alternative to Synergy.

Summary of Recommendation

Stick to Apple Universal Control. It is free, built-in, and solves the hardware limitation of your specific mouse model.
